documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department, visit 04/17/2025
Patient: Bernard Bennett, 69 M

Chief complaint: blood in urine.

HPI: This morning he saw red urine at the start of urinating that cleared by the end of the stream. One episode so far. History of urethral stricture dilated in 2019. No injury, no heavy exercise. No flank pain, fever or dysuria.
PMH: urethral stricture, BPH, hypertension, CKD, primary myelofibrosis on ruxolitinib, chronic bronchitis, Paget disease of left tibia, lumbar spondylosis.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg PRN; reports tamsulosin and lisinopril as well; ruxolitinib 5 mg BID; vitamin D. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 78, afebrile.
Exam: Abdomen soft, nontender, no flank tenderness. GU: prostate mildly enlarged, nontender on rectal exam. Meatus without discharge or lesions.

Results: UA with red cells present (blood moderate, 35 RBC/hpf), no casts, nitrite and leukocyte esterase negative. Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL. CBC at his known baseline per his hematology history, unchanged. PT/INR within normal range.

MDM: Initial hematuria, which points to a urethral source, in a man with a known stricture. Kidney function stable. No clot retention; voided comfortably here.
Disposition: home. Outpatient urology for cystoscopy and upper tract imaging. Return for clots, inability to void, fever.

Emergency medicine

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: hematuria. CT urogram protocol: unenhanced, nephrographic and excretory phases.
Kidneys: normal size and enhancement, no mass, no stones. No hydronephrosis. Collecting systems and ureters opacify fully without filling defect. Bladder: well distended, no wall thickening or filling defect. Prostate enlarged.
Spleen enlarged, as known from prior imaging. Liver normal. No adenopathy. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: No renal mass, hydronephrosis or urothelial filling defect. Enlarged prostate. Known splenomegaly.

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology, 05/13/2025
Re: Bernard Bennett

Mr. Bennett returns to us, last seen for dilation of a bulbar urethral stricture in August 2019. He had one episode of initial hematuria on 4/17, seen in the ED, none since. Voiding adequately, no retention.
Meds: tamsulosin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, ruxolitinib, vitamin D. NKDA.

CT urogram 5/6: no upper tract or bladder lesion.

Flexible cystoscopy today under topical anesthesia: short bulbar urethral stricture, narrow but the scope passes; the mucosa at the stricture is friable and oozes slightly on contact. Prostatic lateral lobes enlarged. Bladder fully inspected: no tumor, no stones, no diverticula. Tolerated well.

Assessment: initial hematuria from a friable recurrent bulbar stricture. Upper tracts and bladder clear. BPH.
Plan: he voids adequately and prefers to avoid another procedure now; observation. Continue tamsulosin. Repeat urinalysis at his primary care office in a few weeks. Return if stream worsens, retention, or further bleeding.

Urology

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department, 10/10/2025
Patient: Bernard Bennett, 70 M

CC: passed out while shaving.

HPI: Over recent months he has had repeated short dizzy spells. This morning, razor at his neck, he felt light-headed, then everything went dark and he came to on the bathroom floor; his wife heard him fall. Out for seconds, no incontinence, no tongue biting, oriented right away. No chest pain or palpitations beforehand. No injury.
PMH: hypertension, CKD, BPH, urethral stricture, primary myelofibrosis (ruxolitinib), chronic bronchitis, Paget disease of left tibia, lumbar spondylosis, age-related cognitive decline.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4, acetaminophen PRN, ruxolitinib 5 BID, vitamin D. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 145/90, HR 78.
Exam: alert, oriented. Neurological exam normal. No carotid bruits. Heart regular, no murmur.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, normal intervals. Troponin normal. BMP normal. CBC at his known baseline.

With continuous ECG and arterial pressure monitoring and atropine at the bedside, carotid sinus massage was performed (right side, 5 seconds; no bruits on auscultation beforehand). It produced a 4-second ventricular pause and a fall in systolic pressure to 85 mm Hg, reproducing his light-headedness. Recovered fully within seconds.

Impression: Syncope due to carotid sinus hypersensitivity, mixed cardioinhibitory and vasodepressor response.
Disposition: observed, ambulating without symptoms, discharged with his wife. Advised to avoid pressure on the neck and tight collars, use an electric razor, and turn his head slowly. Cardiology referral via his primary care. Return for recurrent syncope.

Emergency medicine

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up from the ED last Friday. ED record reviewed: syncope while shaving, carotid sinus massage reproduced it with a 4 s pause and SBP 85. Carotid sinus hypersensitivity.
Since then: no further spells. Bought an electric razor, wearing shirts open at the collar. Wife shaken but fine.
He says he had been having short dizzy spells for a while and hadn't mentioned them.
Exam: vitals as charted, no orthostatic change sitting to standing. Heart regular. Neuro nonfocal.
A/P
1. Carotid sinus hypersensitivity with one syncope. Cardiology referral placed. Reinforced head-turning, collar and razor precautions.
2. HTN: office reading as charted. Holding off adding anything until cardiology weighs in given the pressure drops.
3. Others stable.

reports.text: Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness. LVEF 60% by biplane method. Normal regional wall motion. Normal right ventricular size and function. No significant valvular disease. Atria normal in size. Aortic root normal. No pericardial effusion. Estimated RVSP normal.
reports.conclusion: Normal echocardiogram. LVEF 60%. No significant valve disease.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, consultation 11/12/2025
Re: Bernard Bennett, 70

Thank you for referring Mr. Bennett after his syncope on 10/10. Carotid sinus massage in the ED reproduced symptoms with a 4-second pause and a systolic drop to 85, a mixed carotid sinus hypersensitivity. He describes recurrent brief dizzy spells beforehand. No recurrence since.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4, ruxolitinib 5 BID, vitamin D, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.
Exam: BP and HR recorded. Heart regular without murmur, carotids without bruit, lungs with scattered wheezes, no edema.
Echo today: normal, LVEF 60%, no significant valve disease.

Assessment: Mixed carotid sinus hypersensitivity with a single syncope.
Plan:
- 14-day ambulatory ECG monitor to look for spontaneous pauses.
- Conservative management: avoid neck pressure and tight collars, electric razor, slow head turns, stay well hydrated.
- No pacemaker now. Pacing would be reconsidered if syncope recurs.

Cardiology

14-day continuous ambulatory ECG recording, 11/14/2025 to 11/28/2025, 13 days 21 hours analyzable.
